newsitem.title: USA: HSN to buy Paul Allen's stake in Ticketmaster.
newsitem.headline: HSN to buy Paul Allen's stake in Ticketmaster.

text.p: HSN Inc., parent of the Home Shopping Network, sprinted into the sports and concert ticket business Tuesday, buying a 47.5 percent stake in Ticketmaster Group Inc. from Microsoft Corp. co-founder Paul Allen for about $209 million in stock.
HSN Chairman Barry Diller said the deal was part of the company's strategy to expand further into electronic commerce.

"The wind is at the back of electronic commerce," Diller told analysts and reporters on a telephone conference call. "In the next several years, the ability to offer it to others, we believe, (will make it) a truly large business."
HSN said Allen will offer about 12.3 million Ticketmaster shares for about 7.2 million Home Shopping shares, giving him an 11 percent stake in HSN.
HSN, which also owns 12 UHF television stations, said it planned to raise its stake in Ticketmaster beyond 50 percent.
HSN's stock rose $1.50 to $28.50 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-afternoon, making the deal worth about $205.2 million.

However, HSN said it had assured Allen a price of at least $209 million and would issue additional stock to him next year if the price of its shares fell below $29 a share for the first 20 consecutive trading days in July 1998.
Ticketmaster Chief Executive Fred Rosen said during the conference call that the two companies' "talents and skills are complementary."

Responding to an analyst's question, Rosen admitted that Ticketmaster's capacity to process tickets is "far from being used." But he added that the company had no warehouse capacity for concert and sports-related merchandise sales. "This gives us a leg up," he said.
The transaction is expected to close in July.
On the conference call, money manager Mario Gabelli criticised both Ticketmaster and HSN for not offering Ticketmaster shareholders a premium.
"This deal stinks," said Gabelli. "How do you justify it for the shareholders of Ticketmaster? It's missing the guts of corporate responsibility."
Gabelli, who owns shares of HSN, was not immediately available for further comment.

Officials from both HSN and Ticketmaster defended the deal. "All of us are interested in creating value for shareholders," Rosen said. "It's an extremely positive development. Over a period of time, it will add more value and more strength to this company."
Analysts viewed the deal as a good step for HSN.

"It's a very intriguing combination," said Ed Hatch, a media analyst at UBS Securities. "HSN has an outstanding and underutilized telephone and credit card processing and product fullfillment capabities. It can probably take Ticketmaster's reach to consumers up to another level."
Hatch said HSN can handle up to 2 million phone calls daily.

HSN said the two companies' operating results would be consolidated for accounting purposes, but they would continue to operate as independent entities, with Allen and other Ticketmaster executives joining Home Shopping Network's board.

Allen, who co-founded Microsoft with Bill Gates in 1975, has interests in numerous technology companies. He also owns the Portland Trail Blazers basketball team and holds an option to purchase the Seattle Seahawks football franchise.

Ticketmaster is the world's leading computerized ticketing service, selling 60 million tickets a year through 2,500 retail outlets, 16 nationwide telephone call centres, licensees, client box offices and an Internet site.

It offers access to tickets for more than 150,000 events a year, including concerts, sports events, performing arts and movies. It also has begun selling merchandise, such as videos and T-shirts, to customers who call for tickets.

The Home Shopping Network, which pioneered the television shopping industry in 1982, currently reaches 70 million households via cable and broadcast station affiliates. It also owns the Internet Shopping Network.
HSN, which is based in St. Petersburg, Fla., is also the parent of Silver King Broadcasting and SF Broadcasting.

Silver King, the sixth-largest television broadcast group in the nation, owns and operates 12 independent UHF stations in 11 major markets and holds minority interests in stations in six major markets.
SF Broadcasting owns and operates VHF Fox affiliates in Honolulu, New Orleans, Mobile, Alabama and Green Bay, Wisc.
